prompt: A plan tests R5 with three cases: one as a student, one as a member, one with five tickets. What does it leave untested?
hint: Which sentence of R5 needs two discounts at once?

choices.text: The full price, with no discount
choices.why: True, and small: rule 8 is easy to add; the bigger gap is elsewhere.

choices.text: The rule for discounts meeting: the largest applies
choices.why: Right: none of the three cases lets two discounts meet.

choices.text: Nothing, since each discount has been seen working
choices.why: Each works alone; the defect in this lesson lives where two meet.

choices.text: The price of Hamlet
choices.why: Every case already pays some price for a show.

prompt: A parking rule has four yes-or-no conditions. How many rules does its full decision table have?
hint: Two raised to the number of conditions.

prompt: Rule 5 of the table: not a student, a member, five tickets. What discount does R5 ask for?
hint: Discounts do not add up.

choices.text: 25%, member and quantity together
choices.why: That is the two added, which R5 rules out by name.

choices.text: 10%, as membership is checked first
choices.why: R5 sets no order between them; it says the largest applies.
Right: 10% and 15% both apply, and the larger one wins.

choices.text: 0%, since two discounts cancel
choices.why: Nothing in R5 cancels a discount.

prompt: Match each piece of R5's table to the part of a decision table it is.
hint: Rows on top, rows below, columns.

prompt: Rules 1 to 4 are collapsed into one column: student Y, the rest "–". What is that a bet on?
hint: The tester cannot see the code.

choices.text: That the code ignores the dashed conditions for students, as R5 does
choices.why: Right: if it handles a student member differently, the one column runs only one path.

choices.text: That students are rare enough not to test
choices.why: Collapsing still tests a student; it tests fewer kinds of student.

choices.text: That 50% is the right figure
choices.why: The figure comes from R5; the bet is about the program.

choices.text: That the eight-rule table had a mistake in it
choices.why: Nothing was wrong with it; collapsing trades cases for an assumption.

prompt: Suppose R5 said nothing about two discounts meeting. Filling in rule 5, what should the tester do?
hint: Who decides what the rule is?

choices.text: Write 25%, as the plain sum is the natural reading
choices.why: That is a guess at the rule, and the case would test the guess.

choices.text: Leave rule 5 out of the table until a defect shows up
choices.why: A column left out is a combination nobody tests.

choices.text: Ask the manager before anybody codes against a guess
choices.why: Right: the table found a gap in the requirement, and the owner of the rule fills it.

choices.text: Write whatever boxoffice charges
choices.why: Then the test can never fail: the program has become its own requirement.

prompt: How does the lesson make the condition "member" false?
hint: R4 lets nobody without an account book.

choices.text: It books with an e-mail that has no account
choices.why: That is refused before any price: "Sign up before you book."

choices.text: It signs up a new account and never confirms it
choices.why: Right: an account that exists and is not a member's.

choices.text: It leaves the student box unticked
choices.why: That sets a different condition, student.

choices.text: It restarts boxoffice between orders, so no account is confirmed
choices.why: A restart brings back the seeded member, confirmed.

prompt: Rule 6: a member, not a student, books 2 tickets for Hamlet at R$ 80,00 each. What total in reais does R5 ask for?
hint: Two tickets, less 10%.

prompt: Why are the expected totals written before any order is placed?
hint: What does a wrong bill look like?

choices.text: The order page does not show the total
choices.why: It does, under the discount line.

choices.text: So the eight orders can be placed faster, without stopping to work anything out
choices.why: Speed is a side effect; the reason is what a number afterwards can hide.

choices.text: A wrong discount looks plausible once you see it
choices.why: Right: afterwards you check that R$ 300,00 looks reasonable, and it does.

choices.text: The theatre's manager signs them off first
choices.why: Nobody signs them; R5 is the source.

prompt: Which of these plans would also have found defect 3, the 25%?
hint: Which plans contain a non-student member buying five?

choices.text: One case per discount: student, member, five tickets
choices.why: None of its three cases lets two discounts meet.

choices.text: The collapsed table of five rules
choices.why: Right: it collapses only the student rules, so member and five-or-more still meet in a column.

choices.text: Rules 1 to 4, all with a student
choices.why: Half price wins there, and it did; the defect needs no student.

choices.text: Boundary values of the quantity, as a non-member: 4 and 5
choices.why: A non-member at five is rule 7, and it passed; the defect needs a member.

prompt: Rule 5 charged 25% off: the member's 10% and the quantity's 15% ___ together, which R5 rules out.
hint: An arithmetic word.

prompt: Which of R6's states are final?
hint: No arrow leaves them.

choices.text: Only used, where the order ends up on the night
choices.why: Cancelled and refunded have no way out either.

choices.text: Used, cancelled and refunded
choices.why: Right: no event leads anywhere from them.

choices.text: Paid and used
choices.why: Paid has two transitions out, to used and to refunded.

choices.text: Reserved, the state each order starts in
choices.why: That is the initial state, the opposite end.

prompt: A library loan has 4 states and 3 events, and 5 valid transitions. How many cells of its state table are dashes?
hint: States times events, less the transitions.

prompt: In the model of R6, what is "before the show starts"?
hint: A transition can need more than its event.

choices.text: A state the order passes through on its way to refunded
choices.why: An order is never in it; it is a condition checked at one moment.

choices.text: An event, like Refund
choices.why: Nobody presses it; time passes.

choices.text: A guard on the refund transition
choices.why: Right: refund needs the event and that condition both.

choices.text: An action the transition carries, like giving seats back
choices.why: An action is what a transition does; this is what it needs.

prompt: Sixteen dashes and time for four. By the harm each would do if it worked, which runs first?
hint: Money back, and seats back.

choices.text: Cancel on an order already cancelled
choices.why: Worst case it says the same thing twice; nothing is lost.

choices.text: Use on a reserved order
choices.why: Letting an unpaid order in is harmful, and it hands nothing back.

choices.text: Refund on a used order
choices.why: Right: money returned for a ticket used, and its seats on sale again.

choices.text: Pay on an order that was refunded, charging it again
choices.why: Charging twice is bad and a customer would notice; it returns no seats.

prompt: What exactly went wrong in the case that used an order and then refunded it?
hint: Two things changed that should not have.

choices.text: The refund was accepted and two seats went back on sale
choices.why: Right: the state moved where the table has a dash, and the action ran with it.

choices.text: The refund was refused with an unclear sentence
choices.why: It was not refused: "Order is now refunded."

choices.text: The order stayed used, but the seats came back
choices.why: The state changed too, to refunded.

choices.text: Paying the order failed, so it was never used
choices.why: Pay and use both worked: "Order is now used."

prompt: Book, pay, use: why could that path never have found defect 4?
hint: What does it never do?

choices.text: It runs too few steps to reach the refund
choices.why: Length is not the point; it could run ten steps and still never press a forbidden button.

choices.text: It presses only buttons the state allows
choices.why: Right: the defect sits in a dash, and no valid path goes through one.

choices.text: It never reads the seats left
choices.why: Reading seats would not help; the refund is never attempted.

choices.text: Use was broken in boxoffice 1.0
choices.why: Use worked: "Order is now used."

prompt: Which of these should boxoffice refuse, by R6's state table? Choose every one.
hint: Find the cell for each.

choices.text: Pay on a paid order
choices.why: Dash: an order is paid once.

choices.text: Cancel on a paid order
choices.why: Dash: a paid order leaves by use or refund.

choices.text: Cancel on a reserved order
choices.why: A transition, to cancelled.

choices.text: Use on a cancelled order
choices.why: Dash: cancelled is final.

choices.text: Refund on a paid order, before the show
choices.why: A transition, with its guard met.

choices.text: Refund on a used order
choices.why: Dash, and boxoffice 1.0 accepts it: defect 4.

prompt: Match each situation to the technique this course would reach for first.
hint: One field, a combination, or a history?

pairs.left: A form field takes an age from 18 to 120
A fee depends on weekend, card holder and over three hours
An account locks after three wrong passwords and unlocks by e-mail
A country field accepts the 27 countries of a list

prompt: Hamlet starts at 20:00. Which refund times test the guard "before the show starts"?
hint: A guard is a line in time; lesson 4 has a technique for lines.

choices.text: 19:00 and 21:00, an hour either side
choices.why: An hour is sixty steps; a guard written a few minutes wrong would pass both.

choices.text: A refund a minute either side of 20:00
choices.why: Right: two-value boundary analysis on the guard, at the smallest step the clock keeps.

choices.text: Any time today, since Hamlet is next week
choices.why: That stays on one side of the line; nothing tests the other.

choices.text: 19:00, when booking closes
choices.why: That is R4's line for booking, not R6's for refunds.

prompt: A tester collapses R5's table into five rules. How many orders does it take to run the collapsed table once?
hint: One per column.

choices.text: Eight, as before collapsing
choices.why: Collapsing removed three columns, and three cases with them.

choices.text: Three, one per condition
choices.why: That is the plan that misses combinations, not the table.

choices.text: Five
choices.why: Right: one order per rule.

choices.text: Two, one student and one not
choices.why: The four non-student rules each need their own order.
